messages:
devon: heads-up — noticed gradual memory growth on long streaming tool-loop traces yesterday. starts small (~20MB/hour) but compounds over multi-hour sessions and reproduces on staging with our long-context harness.

aj: repro steps? which branch / runtime flags?

devon: repro script: run-stress-longchat.sh hitting the streaming endpoint with tool-calls enabled, seq_len ~32k over sessions. uses kernel-selection=auto, batching=max.

li: saw something similar last week. profiler shows growing resident set pinned to kv-slab pages. not typical refcount leaks — looks like pages get marked live but idle.

sam: can you paste the flamegraph snippet?

rachel: ops-bot posted a memory snapshot from the failing run: 
```
Resident: 9.6GB -> 12.4GB over 4h
KV slab pages: 3.1GB -> 5.2GB
Pinned slots: 42k -> 87k
Callstack sample (top):
  runtime::kv::page_hold
  runtime::kv::mark_live
  runtime::stream::append_prefix
  runtime::session::tool_loop
```

devon: attaching a short perf sample we took (n=100 samples, 10s):
```
# alloc histogram
0-1ms: 40%
1-5ms: 35%
5-20ms: 15%
>20ms: 10%

# hotspot symbols:
kv::evictable_scan
kv::acquire_page
kv::pin_page
```

aj: interesting that evictable_scan is in the top hotspots — suggests sweep path isn't completing or is being bypassed. could be a race with the streaming path holding temporary refs.

li: hypothesis: our batching heuristic in streaming mode increases prefix reuse, which creates long-lived soft refs into the KV cache. Combined with the allocator's aging window the sweep doesn't target recently referenced pages, so they accumulate.

sam: can we force a more aggressive sweep frequency on the staging pool? config key: kv.sweep_interval_ms (default 300000). try 60000 and see.

devon: tried 60s earlier — reduced growth rate but didn't eliminate it. also saw fragmentation increase (many small free ranges).

rachel: fragmentation + high pinned count could explain RSS growth without obvious leaks. do we coalesce free slabs on sweep?

li: coalescing happens but only when adjacent free slots are seen in the same slab pass. If the free pattern is interleaved (many small evictions between live pages), coalescing doesn't reduce metadata overhead.

aj: next experiment idea: toggle kernel-selection to prefer compact-kernel path that reduces per-page metadata for KV (flag: --kernel=compact). compact kernel trades a slight latency penalty for denser page packing.

devon: ran compact kernel for 2h with same load: RSS plateaued ~10.8GB vs 12.4GB baseline. pinned slots still up but fragmentation measured via slab-buckets dropped ~35%.

sam: promising. caveat: compact path does extra memmove on page reuse which may increase CPU; need throughput check. any perf regression?

devon: p99 latency bumped 3% in stress test, throughput unchanged. good trade for long-lived sessions.

li: still want to understand root cause — why are pages being pinned for so long? stack suggests session::tool_loop retains refs while waiting on external tool completions. long tool latency keeps refs alive.

rachel: do we have per-tool timeout telemetry? some customers' toolchains have 20-30s tails. if tool SDK waits synchronously, that would keep KV refs across delays.

devon: added a protection in the harness to drop soft refs before calling external tool (weakize_prefix_refs()). initial runs show 50% decrease in pinned slots during blocking periods.

aj: so mitigation options: 1) prefer compact kernel for long-session classes, 2) shorten sweep interval / force coalescing, 3) change tool integration to weak refs + explicit re-acquire on resume.

sam: also consider a TTL on cached prefixes for streaming sessions (shorter than general cache TTL). could be per-route config.

li: quick note on eviction: current LRU uses per-session touch timestamps, and our batching heuristic touches prefixes aggressively (to favor reuse). For long context where reuse is lower, touch churn prevents eviction. Maybe change heuristic to touch only on actual token reuse rather than prefetch.

devon: I can spin up an A/B test: route A uses current heuristic, route B uses conservative-touch. collect kv-residency, fragmentation, and p99 latency for 24h.

rachel: please include synthetic long-tool-tail scenarios and real traffic sample. ops-bot can provision a dedicated pool for the A/B run.

ops-bot: created pool "kv-aging-abtest-2026" with 8x GPU workers, retention=24h. link: https://console/redwood/pools/kv-aging-abtest-2026

sam: checklist for the experiment:
- devon: deploy conservative-touch branch to route B
- devon: enable compact-kernel toggle for a second sub-route to measure combined effect
- li: add fragmentation and pinned-slot metrics to the dashboards (kv.pinned_slots, kv.free_ranges, kv.slab_util)
- rachel: run the long-tool-tail synthetic harness
- aj: capture perf + memory flamegraphs hourly

devon: started canary deploy to route B now. I'll post early metrics in this thread in ~2h.

li: if we get clear reduction with conservative-touch, we should make it the default for streaming/tool-loop routes and expose an override.

sam: also file a perf regression ticket for compact-kernel if we see >5% latency impact under typical traffic.

devon: update: 2h in, p95 latency roughly same, p99 +2%, kv.pinned_slots down 40%, slab fragmentation down 30%, RSS slope nearly flat. this looks like the right path.

rachel: great. next steps: production rollout plan, config gating by route, and docs on memory/behavior tradeoffs.

aj: add an integration test that simulates tool-blocking to catch regressions in future kernel changes.

devon: will open PRs: 
- conservative-touch heuristic + test
- compact-kernel opt-in flag
- harness weakize_prefix_refs instrumentation
- dashboard panels + alert if kv.pinned_slots > 70k for 1h

sam: thanks all — good triage and solid experiments. :thumbsup:
